name: Aman Kyoto
positioning: Secluded forest-garden hotel in the northern hills of Kyoto, with minimalist pavilions and onsen bathing
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet garden retreat near Kinkaku-ji rather than a central Kyoto base
Guests who enjoy onsen bathing, tea and Japanese cuisine

facts.text: The Golden Pavilion (Kinkakuji), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is within walking distance of the hotel.
The pavilions were designed by Kerry Hill Architects in a minimalist style.
The grounds include a moss garden dedicated to the late designer Kerry Hill.
Rooms have a very large hinoki bathtub.
Each afternoon, guests are invited to a bowl of premium matcha with seasonal sweets.
Guests are offered complimentary evening aperitifs, from Champagne and wine to sparkling sake.
The Japanese breakfast offers a choice of Kuroge Wagyu beef or grilled fish with clay pot rice or soymilk porridge.
Electric bicycles are available for exploring the neighbourhood's lanes.
A guided tour of the secret garden is offered to guests.
Children's activities include origami and acorn and leaf hunting art sessions, and kids menus are available.

highlights.text: Aman Kyoto was Kerry Hill's last project before he passed away.
The hotel is set in a secret garden in a forest, a stone's throw from Kinkaku-ji Temple.
The spa has outdoor and indoor onsen hot spring bathing facilities.
Taka-an is the hotel's second restaurant, offering a modern kaiseki experience at a long wooden counter.

considerations.text: The hotel is not ideal for guests who want all the sights on their doorstep.
The spa has three private treatment rooms.
The paths are uneven stone, but several rooms close to the entrance are designed for wider accessibility.

sources.title: Aman Kyoto review - Condé Nast Traveler
